results.content: led to a degree of supply chain reconfiguration in the U.S. – away from ‘just-in-time’ models centered around stock being delivered as and when required, towards ‘just-in-case’ strategies based on holding more inventory. Pandemic-triggered restrictions left ‘just-in time’ models exposed. With minimal onsite inventory, overseas-based suppliers and disrupted global trade flows, companies from a range of sectors had little option but to curtail activity. To prevent this from reoccurring, [...] from reoccurring, businesses are looking to hold more inventory which requires more space – holding more stock is believed worth the extra cost if it helps to retain customer loyalty; it also acts as a hedge against rising inflation. Rising transportation costs and delays across the supply chain, both indirect effects of the pandemic, are also encouraging businesses to rethink strategies.
